title: the output cursor was advanced for an OBU that was skipped instead of the input cursor
lifetime_ender: NONE -- the buffer is alive throughout. SPATIAL row.
shape: a skip that advances the wrong cursor, so the destination offset outruns the buffer
allocator_layer: the platform allocator itself: one direct av_malloc-family allocation, no inner layer. FFmpeg's av_malloc is malloc plus alignment.
fidelity: model consumer, real arithmetic: the sizes and the crossing expression are upstream's, quoted in PROVENANCE.md.
live_proof: absent at the pin: n9.0.1:libavformat/rtpdec_av1.c advances `buf_ptr += obu_size;` on the skip path. The form advancing `pktpos` is at 18761f9fb55c^ and is absent from the pin.

cheribsd-revocation.oracle: MEASURED 2026-10-08, results/2026-10-08-cheribsd/: **CAUGHT.** signal=34, si_code=1 (the BOUNDS code), fault at 0x102154, with supervise resolving `expect ffh_write_probe_u8 0x10213c` from the ELF independently of the run -- the fault lies inside the probe's extent, the offset being the -O0 frame setup, and the RANGE is the attribution criterion rather than equality with the symbol address. The crossing leaves the allocator's USABLE size, which is what malloc bounds the capability to, so there is no size-class slack for it to hide in. tools/size-class-audit.py predicted this reading from the measured request size alone, and the two agree.

status: built 2026-10-08; native arms measured by runners/run-native.sh in the same commit. The platform arms are declared predictions.
nested_why: the crossed buffer came straight from av_malloc / av_mallocz / av_calloc / av_malloc_array -- which on the platform is malloc -- with no AVBufferPool or AVRefStructPool between it and the request. So under this inventory's axis, WHO ALLOCATED THE OBJECT, this row is NOT nested.
distinguishing: the two cursors are the only difference: no byte is written for the skipped OBU, yet the DESTINATION offset jumps by its size, so the buffer is overrun by exactly the amount that was never written into it. A variable-name confusion, which is why the fix changes one identifier and nothing else.
